title: Finite presentation over a finite-field polynomial ring
statement: For every prime power \(q\) and integer \(n\geq3\), determine finite presentability of \(\mathrm{SL}_n(\mathbb F_q[t])\).
status: Resolved: no at \(n=3\); yes at every \(n\geq4\), for all finite fields.

title: Finite presentation over a finite-field Laurent ring
statement: For every finite field \(\mathbb F_q\) and integer \(n\geq2\), determine finite presentability of \(\mathrm{SL}_n(\mathbb F_q[t,t^{-1}])\).
status: Resolved: no at \(n=2\); yes at every \(n\geq3\), for all finite fields.

title: Coherence of SL3(Z)
statement: Is every finitely generated subgroup \(H\leq\mathrm{SL}_3(\mathbb Z)\) finitely presented?

title: Coherence of SL2(Z[1/p])
statement: For every prime \(p\), is every finitely generated subgroup of \(\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb Z[1/p])\) finitely presented?
status: Open unconditionally; the Greenberg--Shalom hypothesis implies a positive answer \citep[Theorem~4.2, version~3]{brody2025commensurator}.

title: Ranks for coherence of GLn(Q)
statement: For which integers \(n\geq1\) is the abstract discrete group \(\mathrm{GL}_n(\mathbb Q)\) coherent?
status: Coherent only at \(n=1\); rational triangular subgroups obstruct every \(n\geq2\) \citep[p.~74]{brody2022trees}.

title: Ordinary p-adic interpolation of modular L-values
statement: For a normalized Hecke eigenform and a prime with unit eigenvalue, construct a bounded p-adic distribution from algebraically normalized rational-cusp periods whose primitive-character Mellin values interpolate the critical twisted L-values, with the Euler root and character conventions specified.
status: As of 9 November 2026: Established in the ordinary scope; \citet[\S9.5 and Theorem~10.2]{manin1973periods}. The repeated September exposition is not a fresh open problem. No unrestricted nonordinary boundedness theorem is inferred.

title: Transcendence of zeta(3)
status: As of 9 November 2026: Ap\'ery\textquoteright s irrationality theorem resolves a weaker property; transcendence is still recorded as unknown in \citet[\S1]{nica2024irrationality}, and no accepted subsequent proof was found. \citet[Theorem~1.6]{lai2026linear} is a recent preprint reporting a weaker linear-independence result; it leaves this transcendence question untouched.

title: Transcendence of Euler's constant (elliptical notebook occurrence)
statement: Is Euler\textquoteright s constant \(\gamma\) transcendental? The notebook\textquoteright s “also unproved” is read with the preceding predicate; the historical attribution is less certain than for zeta(3).
status: As of 9 November 2026: Even irrationality is unresolved in the accepted literature checked; \citet[Conjectures~1.0.1--1.0.2 and \S3]{lagarias2013euler}. Purported isolated proofs in search results are not adopted as established results.

title: Representability of every modular lattice by submodules
statement: Is every modular lattice isomorphic to the lattice of all submodules of some module over some ring?
status: As of November 2026: false. Submodule lattices are Arguesian; non-Desarguesian projective-plane lattices are modular and not Arguesian. This obstruction predates the 1973 talk \citep{jonsson1954modular,herrmanntakach2005subgroup}.

title: Classification of finite-dimensional r-subspace systems
statement: For a field \(k\) and fixed \(r\), describe all ordered systems \((V;E_1,\ldots,E_r)\) of subspaces in a finite-dimensional \(k\)-space up to simultaneous linear isomorphism, equivalently the finite-dimensional representations of \(D^r\).
status: As of November 2026: the algebraically closed-field classification is finite for at most three subspaces and tame for four; five subspaces already encode arbitrary matrix pairs. Earlier occurrences are special cases of this general problem. This is distinct from the deformation question GP-1970-23 \citep{gelfandponomarev1971quadruples,bernsteingelfandponomarev1973coxeter}.

title: The conic triple in polynomial and entire-function rings
statement: For \(c=z_1^2+z_2^2-1\), do there exist \(f_1,f_2\) in the specified function algebra such that \((z_1+cf_1,z_2+cf_2)\) generates its unit ideal? The coefficient field and function algebra are part of the question; the notebook's ``common divisor'' is an imprecise formulation.
status: As of 9 November 2026: affirmative over \(\mathbb C[z_1,z_2]\), hence for complex entire functions and the algebra of entire functions of finite exponential type, by the certificate checked in the critical appendix. Negative for real-valued continuous coefficients on the real disk. Brudnyi's later general theorem settles unrestricted entire reduction. No unresolved C/D contribution is inferred from the notebook's missing coefficient restriction.

title: Serre's problem for projective modules over a polynomial ring
statement: For a field \(k\) and finite \(n\), is every finitely generated projective \(k[x_1,\ldots,x_n]\)-module free? This occurrence announces the case \(n=3\) without recording its then-needed field restriction.
status: As of 9 November 2026: solved affirmatively by Quillen and Suslin in 1976. The 1974 Vaserstein--Suslin announcement proves the three-variable case for perfect fields or characteristic different from two. The statement of the general modern theorem must not erase that historical distinction.

title: Monotonicity in a Hill spectral band
statement: For real smooth periodic \(u\), prove \(d_{\lambda}(\lambda)\ne0\) on \(\{|d|<1\}\), where \(d=\frac12\operatorname{tr}M\).
status: As of 9 November 2026: A classical affirmative result; the seminar requested a proof. Closed-gap endpoints are excluded from the derivative assertion.

title: Supplementary data for the periodic inverse spectral problem
statement: For real periodic \(u\), determine what data in addition to the Hill discriminant reconstruct \(u\), with basepoint fixed.
status: As of 9 November 2026: Affirmatively solved in particular by band edges plus a sheet-labelled Dirichlet divisor in the finite-gap class; the cited verification here is limited to that match.

title: Approximation by finite-gap periodic potentials
statement: Is the set of real periodic finite-gap Hill potentials dense among real periodic potentials? The precise modern version uses the \(H^m\) norm for each \(m\ge0\).
status: As of 9 November 2026: Yes; finite-gap potentials are dense in every \(H^m\), \(m\ge0\). The original notebook omitted the topology.

title: Recursive construction of KdV Lax operators
statement: Given \(L=-D^2+u\), construct a normalized odd-order \(A_n\) for which \([A_n,L]\) is multiplication, and relate the resulting hierarchy to conserved-density recursions.
status: As of 9 November 2026: The formal hierarchy and its dressing construction are established. The seminar's additional question about unspecified other equations is not a universal classification problem.

title: Soliton collision phase shifts
statement: For a real pure KdV two-soliton solution with distinct positive wave parameters and fixed scattering data, compute the outgoing minus incoming intercept of each soliton center.
status: As of 9 November 2026: The logarithmic pairwise shifts are established; the source itself calls the scattering answer standard.
